Matches the file. Beyond the earlier fixes it adds sv-set and s-vs. sv-set: "has/have a Save characteristic of 2+" is read (bearer, "models in that unit", "it has … 3+"). Its said accepts a stat mark: Blood-forged Armour (big-demons-baby/master-of-executions) is covered by its Sv mark and is flagged once the mark is removed. That is the only change in the false-positive run, and it is not a false positive. s-vs: "subtract 1 from the Strength characteristic" and "-1 Strength" of an attack that targets, or is allocated to, this unit / the bearer are read, and the unit's own attack on a MONSTER is not. Noted only, both stricter and not in today's texts: (1) sv-set also reads another unit's save, e.g. "If the target has a Save characteristic of 3+, add 1 to the Wound roll". (2) s-vs misses "this unit is targeted by an attack". Strip test, by ability over all lists: 157 flagged, against 156 without the additions (+Blood-forged Armour), and none lost.

Matches the file. Both additions work on their target cases: "if that attack has the [LETHAL HITS] ability, that ability does not apply", "that enemy unit loses the Lethal Hits ability", and "Each time an attack targets this unit, add 1 to the Hit roll" are no longer bonuses. They change no current sentence (0 diffs, 0 gaps). But each one drops the unit's OWN bonus in plausible wordings, and a dropped bonus is a hole in the gate. Tested, missed today: (1) The lost-ability test runs over the whole sentence and matches any "lost … ability". So "If this model has lost one or more wounds, its melee weapons have the [LETHAL HITS] ability." gives nothing, and neither does the same sentence without the comma. "… that enemy unit cannot use the Feel No Pain ability, and this unit's weapons have [LETHAL HITS]", "… have [LETHAL HITS], and enemy units within 6\" lose the Stealth ability" and "models in that unit have the Lethal Hits ability; if this model is destroyed, that unit loses this ability" also give nothing. (2) The drawback test uses SELF, which also covers "that unit", "that model", "it" and "your unit", and it exempts only "this unit/model makes". So a friendly attack on the chosen enemy loses its +1: "each time a friendly ADEPTUS ASTARTES model within 6\" makes an attack that targets that unit, add 1 to the Wound roll" and "each time a model in that unit makes an attack that targets that unit, add 1 to the Hit roll" both give nothing. It also misses the enemy's "a ranged attack targets this unit, add 1 to the Hit roll" and "an enemy unit makes a ranged attack that targets this unit", which are stricter only. The fix does three things. It tests the drawback only on attacks that target this unit / this model / the bearer (ranged or melee too), unless a non-enemy unit or model makes the attack. It reads grants clause by clause, dropping a clause that says lose / lost / cannot use … ability (within 30 characters) or "… does not apply" in that clause or the next. And it does not split at a comma inside a bracket. Tested on 23 cases (all as expected, including "[LETHAL HITS: non-MONSTER, non-VEHICLE]" and "[ASSAULT], [HEAVY] and [LETHAL HITS]"). Over the 490 current sentences it gives 0 differences from the current code and 0 gaps, and the strip test is unchanged (157 flagged).
